pages.text: "Moya, time to splash!" Mom stepped into the shallows. Moya had raced on red dirt all day, but wriggled at the thought of water. "I don't want to. I want to keep running."
"I hate cold water! I hate splashes in my face!" Moya ran behind the reeds. "I'm not going in!" Mom smiled a little.
Among the reeds, Moya felt gritty and itchy. Red dirt covered their stripes, turning the white ones yellow. "What's happened to my stripes?" Moya scratched their side against the reeds.
Through the reeds, Moya saw Tumba, the mud-play champion, splashing. Mom called, "How about an adventure in Splash Land?" Moya poked their head out. "Splash Land? What's that?"
Mom splashed a front hoof in shallow water. Drops sparkled in the sun. Tumba rolled, loosening mud, and circles spread across the water. "Sparkling drops!" Moya craned their neck.

Mom whispered, "Splash Land has steps! Splash your hooves—a waterfall! Roll on your sides—off comes dirt! Shake yourself—sparkles!" Tumba called, "Splash, splash, roll and roll!" Moya stamped eagerly. "Let's do it!"
Moya jumped into the shallows. Splashing hooves made a waterfall of drops. Rolling on their side loosened the dirt. Splashing with Tumba was fun, too! Splash, splash, roll and roll!
Out of the water, Moya shook. Sparkling drops flew everywhere! The gritty feeling vanished and their black-and-white stripes shone. "Water play is this much fun?" Moya whinnied. They had done it!
Now Moya knew Splash Land's steps. "One, hoof-splash waterfall! Two, roll the dirt off! Three, shake and sparkle!" The next evening, Moya ran to the water first. "Let's visit Splash Land again!"
Mom nuzzled Moya's fluffy, dry back. "So clean and shiny!" Water play wasn't something Moya hated anymore. It was the most exciting game! Splash, splash, roll and roll!
